name: Adaptive Survival
description: 1.1.18 plus the turn planner (rev 4): whole-turn lines scored by expected fight HP loss = HP lost now + sum over enemies of (damage/turn x turns left), with per-enemy damage priors from recorded fights, a death penalty, Slippery stacks as effective HP, modeled potions (9 HP use cost), Dark Shackles and Body Slam. Shown to Jev as a prompt line; among Jev-plausible actions it overrides Jev when that saves >= 1 HP. Jev's own potion picks, powers and unmodeled cards stay Jev's call. Rev 4 adds The Insatiable's Sandpit (end each turn at 2+, Frantic Escape +1).

modules.name: Vantom
modules.prompt:
Vantom (173 HP) runs a FIXED 4-turn cycle; identify where you are from its intent: Ink Blot (single ~7) -> Inky Lance (2 hits of ~6) -> DISMEMBER (one ~26 hit + 3 Wounds into your discard) -> Prepare (Buff intent: NO attack, it gains +2 Strength) -> repeat, every attack +2 per completed cycle (Dismember 26, then 28, then 30). Starts with 8 Slippery: each hit that gets through deals only 1 and removes one stack, so the first 8 hits are for stripping — use cheap/multi-hit/0-cost attacks (Anger, Twin Strike, Sword Boomerang), save big single hits until Slippery is 0. Vulnerable applied during Slippery still lasts. Turn plan: Prepare turns are FREE — spend all energy on damage, no Block. Dismember turns are where runs die — Block to cover the full hit (check the numeric warning) and only attack with what is left. On Ink Blot/Lance turns the hits are small: block what is cheap and push damage. Drink lasting Strength/Dexterity potions on turn 1. Wounds are unplayable clutter: exhaust them when a card lets you choose. The real clock is the Strength growth, so every free Prepare turn must be full damage.
Always apply the numeric LETHAL/SEVERE checks when they appear.
modules.rationale: All 4 Vantom deaths in jev-ironclad-117 came on turns 7, 10 and 11: the 28/30 Dismember turns and the ~20-damage Lance turn after Strength stacked. Cycle read from Vantom.cs (InkBlot->InkyLance->Dismember->Prepare(+2 Str)).

modules.name: Ceremonial Beast
modules.prompt: First check lethal against the last enemy before Block. Plow is an HP threshold: unblocked damage that leaves the Beast at or below its current Plow amount stuns it and removes its Strength and Plow. Compare current HP minus that threshold with your available damage; partial progress does not interrupt. Beast Cry applies Ringing: after your first card play that turn, Ringing-afflicted cards cannot be played. Plan that first card for the largest useful effect; do not start with a low-value setup card expecting to play several more. Read current powers and legal actions because the fight changes after the stun.
modules.rationale: User-requested self-contained definitions of Plow and Beast Cry/Ringing. This fight was not reached in the baseline; this correction is sourced from the installed rules, not claimed playtest evidence.

modules.name: Byrdonis
modules.prompt:
Byrdonis (~83 HP) gains +1 Strength at the end of EVERY one of its turns (Territorial), and alternates Swoop (one ~17 hit, first turn) and Peck (3 hits of ~3), each growing by 1 per hit per turn. The fight gets strictly worse every turn, so damage now is worth more than damage later — but Swoop turns are the big single hits: Block the Swoop turns fully; on Peck turns (three small hits) block only what one cheap Block card covers and put the rest into damage. Weak (if you have it) cuts all of its hits. Drink lasting Strength/Dexterity potions turn 1.
Always apply the numeric LETHAL/SEVERE checks when they appear.
modules.rationale: Byrdonis averaged 22.8 HP lost (10-38) over 5 fights in jev-ironclad-117. Cycle read from Byrdonis.cs; Territorial = +1 Str after each of its turns.

modules.name: Phrog Parasite
modules.prompt: Check whether an offered attack kills an enemy before spending energy on Block. Phrog Parasite alternates adding Infection to discard and a four-hit Lash. Killing it spawns four Wrigglers; that is not victory. Wrigglers start stunned: spend that window killing them or setting up efficient damage, not gaining Block against zero incoming damage. Focus on removing a Wriggler that would otherwise attack; consider area damage. Play temporary Strength before other attacks and prefer damage-plus-Block over equal-cost equal-Block defense when there is no harmful attack trigger.
modules.rationale: Baseline died on floor 12 after taking excessive elite damage. Explicitly separates parasite phase from stunned Wriggler cleanup and tells the stateless model what to do during that window.

modules.name: The Insatiable
modules.prompt: Sandpit rules (from its power/card text): Sandpit starts at 4 and loses 1 at the start of each enemy turn; if it reaches 0 you are killed outright, whatever your HP or Block. Liquify shuffles 6 Frantic Escape cards into your piles: each play gives +1 Sandpit, and that card's cost rises by 1 every time it is played. End every turn with Sandpit at 2 or more (play Frantic Escape first when it is at 1, and ideally when it is at 2 and energy allows); otherwise spend everything on damage and on Blocking Lunging Bite. Cycle (read from its intent): opens with Liquify Ground (no attack; adds 6 statuses), then repeats Thrash (2 hits of ~8) -> LUNGING BITE (one ~28 hit) -> Salivate (no attack, +2 Strength). Bite turns are the killers: Block them fully. Salivate turns are free: all damage. Sandpit is a lethal countdown, not ordinary damage that Block can solve. Prioritize ending the fight before it expires. Read generated card effects for any way to extend the countdown; only take setup that pays back before the deadline. Balance Lunging Bite/Thrash defense against the damage race and spend damage potions early enough to matter. Use the observed intent values and current card/power text over fixed damage assumptions.

modules.name: Decimillipede
modules.prompt: On turn 1, before your first attack, drink a held lasting Strength/Dexterity potion (Fysh Oil, Strength Potion, Dexterity Potion) — this fight runs long enough for it to pay off repeatedly. Segments reattach after being downed. Coordinate damage so all segments can be defeated before revivals, using area damage and finishing low-HP segments close together. modules.name: Entomancer
modules.prompt: Cycle: Pheromone Spit (no attack; gains Personal Hive/Strength) -> Bees (7 small hits of ~3) -> Spear (one ~18 hit) -> repeat, stronger each cycle. Bees turns: 7 hits are each reduced by Block, so Block is very efficient. Pheromone turns are free damage turns (prefer your biggest single hits). Personal Hive adds Dazed to draw when powered attacks hit it; repeated small hits, including multi-hits, can flood future hands. Prefer damage per hit and non-attack damage where available, and avoid chip attacks with poor payoff. Hive and Strength ramp over time, so balance that restraint with a prompt kill; do not block indefinitely while the deck clogs. Use the observed intent values and current card/power text over fixed damage assumptions.

modules.name: Infested Prisms
modules.prompt: Cycle: Jab (~15) -> Radiate (~11 and it gains ~11 Block) -> Whirlwind (several small hits of ~5) -> Pulsate (~8 and it gains ~20 Block) -> repeat. It keeps gaining Block, so hit hardest on turns right after its Block drops (Jab/Whirlwind turns) and Block the multi-hit Whirlwind. Vital Spark afflicts Skills with Tainted, and playing affected Skills applies Tainted to you, adding damage to each powered hit received until the enemy turn ends. Multi-hit intents make this especially costly. Compare each defensive or draw Skill against its displayed penalty rather than automatically playing it. Pulsate increases the pressure while attacking and blocking. Favor efficient attacks or other damage sources, and only pay the Skill penalty when survival or a strong payoff justifies it. Use the observed intent values and current card/power text over fixed damage assumptions.

modules.name: Boss fight
modules.prompt: Plan for a long fight: establish sustainable damage and defense without taking avoidable early damage. Compare scaling setup against the current attack. Spend consumables when they materially improve survival; do not hoard through lethal.
modules.rationale: Sustained scaling matters more than preserving every consumable.

modules.name: Elite fight
modules.prompt: Treat health as a scarce resource. Identify the most dangerous visible threat and compare a fast kill against blocking. Use potions aggressively when they prevent substantial damage or a dangerous additional turn.
modules.rationale: Dangerous fights need a different resource policy than routine encounters.

modules.name: Multiple enemies
modules.prompt: Focus affordable threat-removing kills. Otherwise block major surviving attacks and use remaining energy to damage one target. Never spread damage needlessly or leave useful energy unspent.
modules.rationale: Full v113 trace: wasted energy, boss drafting gaps, and skipped potion.

modules.name: Normal encounter
modules.prompt: Make damage progress while preserving HP. Use defense against incoming damage, then spare energy on attacks. Use safe turns for damage/setup. Check kill before spending energy on Block.
modules.rationale: Full v113 trace: wasted energy, boss drafting gaps, and skipped potion.

modules.name: Pending card choice
modules.prompt: Read selection PURPOSE: adding to hand means fetch a card you can use now, NOT discard/exhaust it. Match remaining energy: fetch a cheap lethal attack or needed Block; avoid an unusable expensive card. For exhaust/discard, instead remove the least useful card for this turn; keep cards needed for kills or Block. Respect min/max and already selected cards. For an upgrade, compare the upgraded effect.
modules.rationale: Revised from complete 1.1.2 traces: explain action purpose and concrete survival decisions.

modules.name: Card rewards
modules.prompt: Read the full current deck and known-boss plan. Early: take immediate useful damage/defense/draw beyond starters. Later: fill missing boss answers, not redundant strengths. For Vantom, Anger/cheap multihits remove Slippery; another expensive single hit does not solve that. Do not assume a combo works: Juggling needs 3 attacks played per turn, difficult with many 2-cost attacks. Skip weak/unsupported additions; do not take every card. Keep the deck able to kill: Act 2 normal enemies have 80-130 HP and the Act 2 boss 321 HP. Count real damage sources beyond starter Strikes (good attacks, AoE, Strength scaling like Inflame/Demon Form). Until you have about 4 of them, prefer a solid attack or scaling card over another Block card. Body Slam, Barricade, Juggernaut and Entrench only pay off with a strong Block engine already in the deck.
modules.rationale: Full v113 trace: wasted energy, boss drafting gaps, and skipped potion. 1.1.14: jev-ironclad-1113-01 drafted Barricade, Equilibrium, Body Slam, Impervious and 2 Armaments with almost no damage and died to Hunter Killer (121 HP) after dealing ~83 damage in 9 turns.

modules.name: Upgrade / remove / transform
modules.prompt: Read the selection purpose first. Upgrade a frequently useful card with a material payoff; remove a liability; transform an expendable card. Consider draw consistency and the deck’s current curve. Do not confuse removal with upgrade.
modules.rationale: Purpose-sensitive permanent deck decisions.

modules.name: Collect rewards
modules.prompt: Collect ALL free gold and relics. If potion space is free, TAKE the offered combat potion before Proceed; saving it costs nothing. Inspect every uninspected CardReward for free, then choose a card or Skip. Do not reopen already declined offers. Discard only to replace a held potion with a better offered one when the belt is full; disposal grants no effect.
modules.rationale: Full v113 trace: wasted energy, boss drafting gaps, and skipped potion.

modules.name: Map route
modules.prompt: Plan along reachable routes, not just the next room. Elites give relics but are the most dangerous rooms: do not choose a path into an Elite when your HP is below 50% of max; between 50% and 70%, only with a strong deck and a potion ready. Prefer routes that pass a rest site shortly before an Elite and before the boss. When HP is low, prefer rest sites, shops, and unknown rooms over monsters and elites. Prefer shops when gold can buy a useful improvement. Reassess after each fight.
modules.rationale: jev-ironclad-117-08 entered an elite at 37/80 and reached Vantom at 47; 117-07 entered an Act 2 elite at 25 HP and died there. Adds explicit HP gates.

modules.name: Shop
modules.prompt: Compare affordable BUNDLES, not just one impressive card. With a starter deck, efficient damage plus Block/draw is valuable: e.g. two useful 1-cost cards may beat one expensive purchase. Buy immediate improvements; avoid unsupported powers. Remove curses or bad cards when better than additions. Save for a better affordable purchase; do not buy merely because affordable. Potion value is HP it can save.
modules.rationale: Revised from complete 1.1.2 traces: explain action purpose and concrete survival decisions.

modules.name: Rest site
modules.prompt: Rest heals 30% of max HP; Smith permanently upgrades one card. HP is the resource that decides boss fights. The rest site right before a boss (Act 1 floor 16, the last rest before the boss room): Rest unless you are at 90%+ of max HP — an upgrade almost never outweighs ~24 HP going into the boss. Elsewhere: Rest when below 60% of max HP. Smith only when at 70%+ of max HP and the upgrade materially changes fights (key damage, block or scaling card). Do not count Burning Blood as preventing death. At high HP, avoid wasted healing.
modules.rationale: jev-ironclad-117-05 chose Smith at 68/80 on floor 16 and died to Vantom with Vantom at 18 HP; ~24 more HP would likely have won. Replaces vague 'rest if HP is too low' wording with explicit thresholds.

modules.name: Event fallback
modules.prompt: Read the actual event text and explicit costs. Value health, gold, deck changes and permanent rewards together. Avoid paying for weak additions. Treat unknown outcomes as uncertain rather than inventing rewards or probabilities.
modules.rationale: Safe fallback until an event has an exact authored module.

modules.name: Other decision
modules.prompt: Choose the legal action that best improves survival and the chance of winning. Use the supplied rules and do not invent hidden information.
modules.rationale: Fail-safe strategy selection; prompt projection still rejects unsupported game decision kinds.

modules.name: Inklets
modules.prompt: Slippery caps the next HP loss to 1, then is consumed. Strip it with a cheap hit before a big attack; never spend 2 energy on a big hit into Slippery when a cheap hit is available. Speed Potion only helps if Block cards are still playable this turn. Kill exposed enemies if affordable; otherwise block the group.
modules.rationale: Revised from complete 1.1.2 traces: explain action purpose and concrete survival decisions.

modules.name: Ruby Raiders
modules.prompt: Raider roles (fixed per type): Crossbow alternates Fire (~14) and Reload (no attack); Assassin hits ~10 EVERY turn; Brute alternates Beat (~7) and Roar (+3 Strength); Axe cycles small Swings and a Big Swing (~12); Tracker applies Frail (your Block cards give less) then hits 8 times for 1 each turn after. Kill order when affordable: Assassin and Crossbow first (the steady big damage), Brute before it stacks Strength; Tracker's 1-damage hits are nearly all absorbed by any Block. Budget the whole turn. Kill the attacker you can actually finish; a large hit that leaves it alive prevents nothing. Bash then a 1-cost attack can beat the reverse order. With no affordable kill, block surviving attacks. Attack freely on buff-only turns.
modules.rationale: Revised from complete 1.1.2 traces: explain action purpose and concrete survival decisions. 1.1.12: roles from the Ruby Raider monster classes; this group cost 23 HP on average over 5 fights in jev-ironclad-117.

modules.name: Spiny Toad
modules.prompt: Spiny Toad (~117 HP) repeats a fixed 3-turn cycle, readable from its intent: Buff (no damage; it gains 5 Thorns at the end of that turn), then a 23-damage Explosion (Thorns still up during YOUR turn, removed after it resolves), then a 17-damage Tongue Lash (no Thorns). While it has Thorns, every attack HIT you land deals 5 damage back to you, taken from your Block first and then HP — so attacking after you Block throws away the Block you raised for the 23, and multi-hit cards (Twin Strike, Sword Boomerang, Spite) are the worst plays. Buff-intent turn: it cannot hurt you, so spend everything on damage (and Vulnerable/setup) now. Explosion-intent turn: Block the 23 and do NOT attack afterwards unless one hit kills it. Lash-intent turn: Thorns are gone, so Block the 17 and put leftover energy into attacks. The damage windows are the Buff and Lash turns.
modules.rationale: jev-ironclad-117-02/03/04: Toad ended two runs and cost 34-40 HP most fights. Recorded fight (117-02 f30): on the Explosion turn the model attacked with Setup Strike, Spite, Anger and Strike, eating 3 Thorns hits (15 HP) on top of the 23 Explosion, dropping 48 -> 10. Its pattern is fully deterministic, so the module states it instead of leaving it to be inferred. 1.1.11: recorded turn shows Thorns consumed Block before HP (blk5 -> Setup Strike -> blk0, HP unchanged), so attacking after blocking wastes the Block.

modules.name: Chompers
modules.prompt: Chompers come as a pair, one started out of phase, so something attacks you nearly every turn. Each has ~62 HP and Artifact 2, which cancels its first two debuffs: do not spend Vulnerable/Weak on a Chomper until Artifact is gone (each application only removes a stack). Each Chomper alternates Clamp (2 hits of 8 = 16) and Screech (no damage, adds 3 Dazed to your discard, which clog later hands). Read intents every turn: block the Clamp hits, and on a turn where the attacker is the one about to Screech, its damage is free. Focus one Chomper to death first — killing it removes its Clamps and its Dazed, which is worth more than spreading damage. Do not open with all-out offense and no Block into a visible 16.
modules.rationale: jev-ironclad-117 Act 2: Chomper cost 11-37 HP a fight (22, 33, 31 lost in three runs). Recorded fight (117-02 f22): turn 1 played four attacks with 0 Block into a 16 Clamp, Bash+ landed on Artifact and was wasted, and the second Chomper's Clamps kept coming after the first died. The encounter is code-defined as a pair with ScreamFirst set on one.

modules.name: Nibbit
modules.prompt: Nibbit (~44 HP) cycles Butt (one ~12 hit) -> Slice (~6 hit and it gains 5 Block) -> Hiss (Buff: NO attack, +2 Strength) -> repeat, each cycle +2 damage. Hiss turns are free damage turns. Block Butt turns fully; Slice turns are cheap to block. It is a normal fight: aim to take under 10 HP. Kill it before its second or third Hiss.
modules.rationale: Most frequent Act 1 fight (13 in jev-ironclad-117) with HP loss 3-29 — wide variance for a simple fixed cycle. Read from Nibbit.cs.

modules.name: Mawler
modules.prompt: Mawler (~72 HP) picks randomly among Rip and Tear (one ~14 hit), Claw (2 hits of ~4) and Roar (applies 3 Vulnerable to you, no damage). While you are Vulnerable, its hits deal 50% more, so after a Roar the next Rip and Tear (~21) is the danger — block those fully. Roar turns are free damage turns.
modules.rationale: Seen 6 times, up to 21 HP lost. Moves read from Mawler.cs (random branch).

modules.name: Shrinker Beetle
modules.prompt: Shrinker Beetle (~39 HP) opens with Shrink (debuffs you, no damage), then alternates Chomp (~7) and Stomp (~13). Turn 1 is a free damage turn. Block Stomps; Chomps are cheap.
modules.rationale: Read from ShrinkerBeetle.cs.

modules.name: Tunneler
modules.prompt: Tunneler (~87 HP): Bite (~13) -> Burrow (gains 32 Block that does NOT expire, plus Burrowed) -> Below (~23) EVERY turn, forever, until its Block is broken. Breaking all of its Block stuns it (it skips its next attack, then returns to Bite). So after it Burrows, the fight is: break the 32 Block as fast as possible — all damage into it — while blocking the 23s. Do not leave it burrowed; it hits 23 every turn. On the Burrow turn itself (no attack), hit it with everything BEFORE it gains the Block if you can make it cheaper to finish.
modules.rationale: Tunneler.cs: Below loops on itself; BurrowedPower keeps its Block and stuns it when the Block breaks. 16-24 HP lost per Tunneler fight in jev-ironclad-117 Act 2.

modules.name: Exoskeleton
modules.prompt: Exoskeletons have Hard To Kill 9: no single hit can deal more than 9 damage to them, so big single-target attacks are wasted — prefer many hits (multi-hit, 0-cost attacks, area damage). They alternate Skitter (3 small hits), Mandibles (~8) and Enrage (+2 Strength). With several, focus one until dead; block multi-hit turns.
modules.rationale: HardToKillPower caps each damage instance at its Amount (9). 3-21 HP lost per fight in Act 2.

modules.name: Myte
modules.prompt: Myte (~64 HP) cycles Toxic (adds 2 Toxic cards to your hand: each deals 5 to you at end of turn if still in hand — Block absorbs that damage, so Block also covers them), Bite (~13), Suck (~4 and it gains +2 Strength). Toxic turn: no attack, so deal damage, and before ending the turn either play the Toxics or hold 5 Block per Toxic left in hand. Block Bites.
modules.rationale: Killed a run at floor 21 (jev-act2-push-04) and cost 27 HP in another. Read from Myte.cs.

modules.name: Louse Progenitor
modules.prompt: Louse Progenitor (~135 HP) alternates Web Cannon (~9 and makes you Frail: your Block cards give 25% less), Pounce (~14) and Curl and Grow (Block, Curl Up, +5 Strength; no attack). It grows +5 Strength each cycle, so this fight must be ended fast — Curl turns are free damage turns (hit through its Block). Block Pounces fully; Frail makes blocking weaker, so plan for it.
modules.rationale: Cost 10-34 HP in Act 2 runs. Read from LouseProgenitor.cs.

modules.name: Thieving Hopper
modules.prompt: Thieving Hopper (~79 HP) opens with Thievery (~17 and steals a card), then Flutter (Buff: halves damage it takes from attacks, one stack removed per attack that gets through), then hits ~21 and ~14, and eventually Escapes with the stolen card. Many cheap hits strip Flutter faster than one big hit. Kill it before it escapes to get the card back; block its 17/21 hits.
modules.rationale: Read from ThievingHopper.cs (FlutterPower 50% reduction; EscapeArtist).

modules.name: Bowlbugs / Slumbering Beetle
modules.prompt: Bowlbug Nectar: attacks, then on its 2nd turn gains +15 Strength, then attacks every turn after — KILL NECTAR FIRST, ideally before that buff. Bowlbug Rock: Headbutt; if its attack is FULLY blocked it becomes off-balance and loses a turn, so fully blocking the Rock is worth it. Bowlbug Silk: 2 small hits or makes you Weak. Slumbering Beetle (~86 HP, Plating 15) starts ASLEEP and does nothing; 3 damaging hits wake it, after which it hits ~16 every turn and gains Strength — do not hit it until everything else is dead, then kill it while fresh.
modules.rationale: Bowlbug group with Slumbering Beetle cost 39 HP in one Act 2 fight. Mechanics from BowlbugNectar/Rock/Silk.cs, ImbalancedPower, SlumberPower.

modules.name: Slimes
modules.prompt: Medium slimes hit hardest (Twig M ~11, Leaf M ~8 alternating with adding statuses to your deck); small slimes hit for 3-4. Kill the medium slimes first, then the small ones; area damage is ideal. Block only when the combined visible attacks are large.
modules.rationale: Slime groups cost 12-18 HP in several Act 1 fights. Moves from LeafSlimeM/TwigSlimeM/LeafSlimeS/TwigSlimeS.cs.

modules.name: Hunter Killer
modules.prompt: Hunter Killer (~121 HP) opens with Tenderizing Goop (no attack): it gives you Tender for the rest of the fight — EVERY card you play this turn gives you -1 Strength and -1 Dexterity until the turn ends. So each later card in a turn is weaker: play Block cards FIRST (before attacks lower your Dexterity), then your biggest attacks; cheap filler cards played late do almost nothing. After the Goop it randomly uses Bite (~17, one hit) or Puncture (3 hits of ~7 = ~21); Bite never twice in a row. Both hurt: Block each attack turn as your first plays, and use a Block/Strength potion early — this fight cost 34 HP when fought without Block ordering.
modules.rationale: HunterKiller.cs + TenderPower.cs: per-card -1 Str/-1 Dex, restored at end of turn. jev-ironclad-1111-01 lost 34 HP (69->35).

modules.name: The Obscura
modules.prompt: The Obscura (~123 HP) opens by summoning Parafright, an Illusion minion (21 HP) that Slams you EVERY turn (~16, growing). Parafright cannot be killed for good: at 0 HP it spends its next turn reviving to full HP instead of attacking. The fight ends the moment The Obscura dies (its minion goes with it). So put your damage into THE OBSCURA, even though Parafright's intent is bigger. Knocking Parafright out only cancels its next Slam; do it only when it takes about one card and its Slam is big. The Obscura itself randomly uses Piercing Gaze (~10), Hardening Strike (~6 and it gains ~6 Block) or Wail (Buff: +3 Strength to its allies, making Parafright's Slam bigger); it never repeats a move twice in a row. Block Parafright's Slam each turn; area damage that also hits The Obscura is fine.
modules.rationale: TheObscura.cs, Parafright.cs, IllusionPower.cs (revive to full HP after a turn; Minion). jev-ironclad-1113-05 died from 80 HP in a 10-turn fight, repeatedly killing Parafright while The Obscura ended at 54/123. 1.1.16: generic multi-enemy hint named Parafright the biggest threat and Jev split damage onto it (jev-ironclad-1115-01 died at floor 30); that hint is now skipped for this module.

ironclad.potion_policy: Take free potions into empty slots. On turn 1 of an elite or boss fight, before your first attack, drink your best lasting Strength/Dexterity potion (Fysh Oil, Strength Potion, Dexterity Potion) if you hold one — do not carry it unused into a fight you might lose. Spend potions to prevent 10+ HP loss or secure kills; if currently safe, you may reserve one useful boss answer, but never hoard through death or a full-belt replacement.

groups.advice: Lasting Strength/Dexterity/Fysh Oil: use early in elites/bosses, before affected cards.
Damage/Block/Vulnerable: prioritize threat-removing kills and HP saved; Vulnerable before damage.
Temporary Strength/Dexterity: use before matching cards; expires this turn.
Attack/Power potion cards are free this turn, even at zero energy. Power is better early in long fights.
Draw/retrieval: use when energy or free effects let you play the result.

compression_contract.target: Under 1000 measured input tokens per model decision on average, not a hard truncation cap.
compression_contract.combat: Current hand/effects once, indexed enemies, powers and intents; compact legal actions; unordered pile name/count summaries. Effects of offered retrieval cards remain in actions. No hidden draw order.
compression_contract.other: Retain deck effects for drafting, shop, route and rest decisions; retain selection constraints and event rules.
compression_contract.limits: Pile cards not currently actionable have names/counts only during combat. Unknown interactions may need targeted expansion. Actual provider token counts and performance must be measured after approval.

combat_basics: Goal: minimize total HP lost this whole run, not just this fight. HP saved now is HP (or a future rest-site heal) you still have later. Turn count itself has no value. Finishing a fight sooner usually reduces total damage taken because most enemies' output escalates turn over turn and your Block draw is not guaranteed — so prefer the faster kill when every turn along the way is safely survivable. But if this turn's queued damage threatens to overwhelm you, block first regardless of tempo: a fight you die in is always worse than a slower win, with no exception. Never take free/affordable Block-worthy damage you could have prevented before spending on pure offense that has no defensive value and doesn't secure a kill this turn. Enemy powers override generic card sequencing.

turn_advice.no_incoming: No enemy attacks now: spend energy on damage/setup, not ordinary Block. Do not end with useful attacks available.
turn_advice.one_energy: With 1 energy: take a kill if possible; otherwise useful Block, otherwise ATTACK. If no Block can be played, damage is better than wasting energy.
turn_advice.under_attack: Compare kill/Weak/Block prevention; avoid buying small chip damage with large HP loss when defense is available. After defensive plays, spend leftover energy on attacks — this turn's damage is within a safe margin, so taking some of it is not a reason to pass on progress.
turn_advice.no_block: No playable card here grants Block. Use attacks/setup with remaining energy rather than End Turn; nonlethal attacks are useful. Check potions too.
turn_advice.slippery: Slippery: each HP-damaging hit removes ONE stack and deals 1 HP. Cheap/multihit attacks are progress, not wasted damage. Strip stacks with spare energy EVERY turn. Do not save attacks only for lethal. Prefer cheap hits over Bash while capped; defend major hits but keep making progress.
turn_advice.lethal_risk: LETHAL THIS TURN AS QUEUED: incoming damage {incoming} vs your HP {hp} and current Block {block} (deficit {deficit}). Unless you raise Block by at least {deficit} before ending turn, this attack kills you. Block is mandatory before any attack that doesn't secure a kill right now. Potions held: {potions}. If one can raise Block, prevent damage, restore HP, or fetch a playable card (a Skill Potion can pull a Block card from nothing even with no Block card in hand right now), use it this turn — do not save it into a fight you lose.
turn_advice.severe_risk: SEVERE: incoming damage {incoming} vs your HP {hp} and current Block {block} (deficit {deficit}) would take you below half HP this turn. Prioritize Block up to what you can afford; only spend leftover energy on damage that secures a kill or clearly shortens the fight. Potions held: {potions}. A held defensive or card-fetching potion is worth using here rather than saving it further.
turn_advice.big_hit: BIG HIT: {deficit} unblocked damage is queued (incoming {incoming}, your Block {block}, HP {hp}). HP lost here carries through the whole run. Play your Block first (and a Weak effect or potion if it saves ~10+), then attack with what is left; only skip Block if your attacks kill the attacker this turn or the Block cards cost far more than the damage they prevent. Potions held: {potions}.

boss_plans.VANTOM_BOSS: Vantom: remove 8 Slippery stacks with cheap/multihit attacks, then burst. Draft a few 0-cost/multihit attacks (e.g. Anger), draw and defense; avoid only expensive single hits. Save a useful attack/draw potion if current fights are safe. Do not refuse a life-saving potion now.
boss_plans.CEREMONIAL_BEAST_BOSS: Ceremonial Beast: build enough burst to cross its Plow HP threshold and stun it; strong single-card effects matter when Ringing restricts follow-up plays. Preserve a useful burst potion if safe.
boss_plans.THE_KIN_BOSS: The Kin: efficient attacks/area damage remove followers; secure damage before Ritual Strength ramps, and enough defense for the priest. Keep a useful damage potion if current fights are safe.
boss_plans.THE_INSATIABLE_BOSS: The Insatiable (321 HP) is a race: it puts you on a Sandpit countdown and you must deal ~320 damage while spending energy on Frantic Escape to stay alive. Draft scaling damage (Strength: Inflame/Demon Form; strong multi-hits with Strength; Rampage), extra energy and card draw; more small Block cards do not win this race. Keep damage/Strength potions for this fight.

mechanic_hints.text: Weak: normally 25% less Attack damage, rounded down per hit. Stacks are duration, not stronger reduction. Use Weak before a large incoming attack; a potion costs no energy, so consider it even just before End Turn. Saving ~7+ HP now is valuable; do not hoard it through the boss.

Vulnerable: normally 50% more Attack damage taken; stacks extend duration. Apply BEFORE follow-up attacks (including free Anger) if the target is not already Vulnerable. Existing debuffs are already included in attack previews: do not multiply twice. Bash setup is not mandatory: prefer immediate lethal or needed Block over setup that exposes you to a huge hit. Slippery caps override this.
Speed Potion: temporary Dexterity boosts Block from cards THIS turn, then expires. Use before useful Block cards; save it if you cannot play any. Energy 0 with no free Block card means no benefit.
Flex Potion: temporary Strength adds damage to EACH Attack hit this turn. Drink before attacks; save it if no attacks remain playable. Slippery can nullify the extra damage.

Exhaust removes a card for this combat; discarding only delays its redraw. For chosen exhaust, prefer an unusable Wound or other low-value card, preserving needed defense/lethal attacks. Exhaust-draw can find answers but consumes energy; do not spend your last energy cycling when a known useful play is better.
Wound is unplayable and clogs future draws. Good chosen-exhaust target; drawing one does not itself hurt HP.
Dazed is unplayable and Ethereal: if held at end of turn it exhausts automatically.
Slimed costs 1, draws 1, and Exhausts. Useful cleanup with spare energy; do not sacrifice necessary defense or lethal for it.
Frail normally reduces Block gained from cards by 25%. Read current card effects; do not apply the reduction twice.
Plating grants its current amount of Block at end of your turn and loses 1 on following turns. Free helpful relics are worth collecting.

Toxic (status card): if still in your hand when your turn ends it deals 5 damage to you, and Block absorbs that damage like an attack. Playing it costs 1 energy and exhausts it. So a Defend (1 energy, 5 Block) prevents the same 5 and also covers enemy attacks: when an attack is incoming, Block first and only play Toxics with spare energy; when nothing attacks, playing a Toxic (or holding Block) avoids the 5.

current_turn_hints.no_speed_target: CURRENT TURN: no Block card is playable. Speed Potion cannot help now: SAVE it. If no useful card or other potion is available, End Turn.
current_turn_hints.large_attack_weak: CURRENT TURN: at least 20 damage exceeds your Block, and you hold Weak Potion. Use Weak Potion on the major attacker NOW before spending energy on damage; it reduces this attack and later attacks during its duration.

multi_enemy_template: MULTI-ENEMY: {count} enemies alive. {top_name} currently queues the most damage ({top_dmg}, {top_hp} HP left). All else equal, remove or block against the biggest current threat first; take a cheap kill on a different enemy only if it's actually available this turn. Prefer an attack that hits all enemies when one is affordable and enemies are roughly even health.
rest_math: Rest-site math: you are at {hp}/{max_hp} HP ({pct}%). Rest would restore only {heal} HP right now. If that is under ~12 HP, Rest is mostly wasted: choose Smith and upgrade your most impactful card (a key attack, Block or scaling card; Bash is a strong default). Choose Rest when it restores a large amount and the HP matters for the next fights, and always before a boss unless you are already near full.
route_summary: Route summary computed from the visible map (paths from each option to the end of this act). Elites give relics but cost HP. Aim for about one Elite per act when HP is 70%+ and the deck is solid, ideally with a rest site before it. Avoid options that force 2+ Elites (the low number is above 1) unless you are at high HP with a strong deck. Below 50% HP, pick an option that can steer to 0 Elites for now.
